open_obligations: Check whether the trained dishonest debater became more deceptive, which would bear on equilibrium safety.
Check whether the Llama3-8B debaters started from an RLHF-tuned model.
Check that the 4-point gain holds across question subsets.
in.other_title: Stronger trained debaters yield +4 points judge accuracy; no effect for consultants
in.rationale: Kenton et al. say inference-only prompting gives little evidence about equilibria reached by training. Arnesen et al. train debaters with DPO and report the fully trained debater is associated with 4 percentage points higher judge accuracy than the SFT model (p < 10^-6), while consultant skill shows no apparent relationship with judge accuracy.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether conclusions from inference-only debate carry over when debaters are trained, on QuALITY-HARD

text: The authors state that their study prompts models to play consultancy and debate roles in an inference-only setting, so it gives little evidence about the safety properties of the equilibria reached by training models in these games, and that all consultants/debaters were RLHF-fine-tuned for honesty, which may hamper the dishonest consultant or debater.
title: Inference-only debate with RLHF-honest models says little about debate as training
